title: Китайская экскурсия и обещание Макса  (The Chinese Tour Group and Max's Promise)

segments.t: Vika rushes into the kitchen in a panic to tell Max that an entire busload of Chinese tourists has just sat down expecting lunch while the Chef is gone and Lyova is on vacation. As Vika grabs her phone to call Nagiyev, Max begs her to trust him to save the service.
Шеф уехал, су-шеф в отпуске, а остальные...
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
'We have guests in the dining room.' Barinov displays a calm approach across the room, putting "gosti" ("visitors, guests") alongside "nas" ("us") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.

'There was supposed to be one and a half people today.' Vika maintains a thoughtful tempo in their talk, putting "cheloveka" ("a man, a person") alongside "dolzhno" ("ought, must") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'A whole tour group just arrived.' Nagiyev offers a brisk line as they talk, weaving "ekskursiya" ("field trip") together with "priyekhala" ("came, arrived") just the way native speakers do.

'Do you understand what kind of situation this is?' Barinov challenges pointedly as the talk turns, weaving "ponimayesh" ("do you understand") together with "delo" ("matter") just the way native speakers do.
Шеф уехал, су-шеф в отпуске, а остальные...

'The Chef left, the sous-chef is on vacation, and the rest...' Vika conveys an earnest line in the room, building the phrase around "uyekhal" ("left, went away") and "su-shef" ("sous-chef") for a crisp, natural delivery.
'Wait, why is that?' Nagiyev presses pointedly from the start, using "pochemu" ("why") by itself, a common way spoken Russian keeps fast dialogue punchy.
'Have you all lost your minds?' Barinov questions dryly with Nagiyev now, anchoring the Russian line on "uma" ("mind") and "soshli" ("went off") without extra filler.
'The acting sous-chef is right here on duty.' Vika shares a resolute stance without hesitation, linking "seychas" ("now"), "su-shef" ("sous-chef"), and "meste" ("place") in one brisk exchange.
'Alright, that is it.' Nagiyev keeps an earnest course across the room, putting "tak" ("so") alongside "vse" ("all") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'I am calling Dmitriy Vladimirovich right now.' Barinov shares an emphatic stance with Vika, pairing "zvonyu" ("call") with "dmitriyu" ("Dmitry") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'Vika, please do not.' Vika picks a thoughtful stance straight away, pairing "nado" ("it is necessary") with "vik" ("Vika") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'Vika, I will solve this problem myself.' Nagiyev shows a firm attitude as they talk, linking "reshu" ("I'll solve"), "problemu" ("problem"), and "vik" ("Vika") in one brisk exchange.
'Trust me, please.' Barinov holds an emphatic tack at this moment, linking "pover" ("believe"), "mne" ("to me"), and "pozhaluysta" ("please") in one brisk exchange.
Шеф уехал, су-шеф в отпуске, а остальные...

That wraps up this scene as with the dining room packed with Chinese tourists and the kitchen short-staffed, Vika reaches for the phone to call Nagiyev, but Max begs her to let him solve the crisis. Until next time!
